newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN NARROWS GAP AGAINST SLUMPING BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN NARROWS GAP AGAINST SLUMPING BAYERN.

text.p: Bayer Leverkusen closed to within a single point of Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich with a convincing 5-0 win over Hamburg before a sell-out home crowd of 22,000 on Sunday.
Led by Ulf Kirsten's three goals, second-place Bayer scored early and often and never looked back.
Leverkusen now have 63 points and trail Bayern who have 64 with three weeks to play. Bayern Munich played to a scoreless draw against last place Freiburg on Saturday.

"This team doesn't need a trainer at the moment -- its functioning superbly by itself," said Bayer Leverkusen trainer Christoph Daum. "Bayern Munich still are in front of us and they can still win it by themselves. But I am convinced we will win the championship."
Bayern Munich president Franz Beckenbauer said earlier his team were not playing well enough to win the championship.
Nico Kovac put Bayer in front in the 10th minute before Kirsten erupted for goals in the 32nd, 49th and 64th minute to give him a league-leading 21 for the season.
Paulo Sergio added a fifth goal in the 70th minute to round off Bayer's eighth consectutive home win.
"We were a sad sight," said Hamburg president Uwe Seeler. "We played very poorly."
